chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj, who said:

I bought a loader, so I gave part of its price and left it with its owner. Then I was detained for a few days, then I came to the seller of the loader to take it, so he said, 'I have sold it.' So I laughed, then I said, 'No, by Allah, I will not let you go, or I will seek judgment against you.' So he said to me, 'Would you be pleased with Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash?' I said, 'Yes.' So we went to him and related our story to him. So Abu Bakr said, 'By whose words do you like that I judge between the two of you, by the words of your companion or someone else?' He said, 'I said, by the words of my companion.' He said, 'I heard him saying: Whoever buys something and brings the price within what is between it and three days, otherwise there is no sale for him.'

key_terms.أُقَاضِيَكَ: I will seek judgment/adjudication from you
key_terms.فِي مَا بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَ: Within the period between now and three days

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a sale where the buyer pays part of the price and has a few days to pay the rest?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated via the chain of Safwan ibn Yahya, establishes the 'khiyar al-shart' (option of condition) in sales, specifically limiting the buyer's right to cancel to a three-day period after partial payment. Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, a prominent early jurist, validates this by citing the Prophet’s tradition that a sale is not final if the full price is not settled within three days, highlighting the Shia emphasis on contractual clarity and the prevention of uncertainty (gharar) in commercial transactions.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Hassan Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said,

‘I bought a loader, so I gave part of its price, and left it with its owner. Then I awaited for a few days, then I came over to the seller of the loader in order to take it, so he said, ‘I have sold it’. So I laughed, then I said, ‘No, by Allah<sup>saww</sup>, I will not let you (do this), or I shall seek judgement over you’. So he said to me, ‘Would you be pleased with Abu Bakr Bin Ayyash (as a judge)?’ I said, ‘Yes’. 
So we went over to him, and we related our stories to him. So Abu Bakr said, ‘By whose words would you like that I judge between the two of you, by the words of your Master<sup>asws</sup> or someone else?’ I said, ‘By the words of my Master<sup>asws</sup>’. He said, ‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who buys something, so either he comes up with the price in what is between it and three days, or else there is no sale for him’.
en.sarwar: 16. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Hassan ibn Al-Husayn from Safwan ibn Yahya from ‘Abd al- Rahman ibn al- Hajjaj who has said the following:

“I once purchased a carriage and paid a certain amount of the price, then left it with the seller. I remained engaged for several days then went to the seller to take possession. He said, ‘I have sold it.’ I laughed and said, ‘By Allah, I will not allow you to do this without asking for a judgment.’ He said, ‘Will you agree to go for judgment before abu Bakr ibn ‘Ayyash?’ I replied, ‘Yes, I agree.’ We went to him and told him about our stories. Abu Bakr asked, ‘On the basis of whose words you want me to decide?’ He (the narrator) has said that I asked him to decide on the basis of the words of my companion (Imam).’ He said, ‘I heard him (Imam) say, “If one brings payment within three days the deal is valid, otherwise, there is no deal in his favor.’”
